description.narrative: This project intends to facilitate the process of raising Baruuli-Banyala youths’ access toland as a tool of agriculture production and access to water foragriculture production through the use of small-scale irrigationtechnologies to facilitate their engagementin offseason productionof horticultural enterprises as sources of incomes. Even when thepiece of land accessed by the youths is small, if this issupplemented by availability of small-scale irrigation facility andproduction of high value commodities, the Baruli and Banyalayouths can earn significant income to meet their needs and families.The project shall form the Banyala and Baruli youths into small peergroups of 5 members, amongst whom at least two shall be femaleyouths. In their groups, the project shall build the capacity oflobbying, advocacy and engagement skills so that they are able toconstructively engage with male adults in their communities thatown land to allow them access to and utilisation of the land forcommercial production of horticulture commodities. A buy-inmechanism to ease this process shall be in-built whereby thelandowners shall derive a share of the benefits raised from the saleof the products from the project managed on their land.

participating-org.narrative:
An organisation that unites all religions, cultural background for development and support of vulnerable people for life longer skills and their self-sustainability. It’s unique in the way that members are recruited from the vulnerable people supported in order to make a strong institution with its members. Rights holders play a part within the organisation such that they know better about their issues than people far from the reality. We advocate with the rights holders for inclusion and management. Unique in action where we believe in community empowerment and self-reliance in all kinds of support and activities initiated. Our motto says “greatest work comes from the community”, which indicate that all the services offered, we initiate them from the community which indicates ownership and sustainability after project life time. We encourage rights holder’s participation and prioritizing on the needful ratherthan thinking for them.
The principal thematic areas are humanity and socio-economic empowerment. BMCDA is open to groups and individuals across Uganda as a country. As the main focus of our work is towards making communities robust and self-driven, a majority of our members come from among groups and individuals that espouse the voluntary spirit and selflessness in serving communities. BMCDA is primarily focused on working with communities to identify their potential and develop capacities to take full charge of their destiny with minimum harm to their surroundings, for enjoyment of present and future benefits. Disadvantage members of the communities are spread across the rural-urban divide and our organisation strives to work with them wherever they are, to build their coping mechanisms and their capacities for better lives.
As an organisation, we are proud of the fight against Covid-19 pandemic of 2021, where we reached out to several households without any excuses. During that time 538 households were reached and changed the status quo that came up with Covid-19. We fought stigma, Discrimination, myths, provided information and appropriate referral to health workers in conjunction with the taskforces both at the sub-county and district level. Some vulnerable households were supported with food stuffs, cloths, mattresses and liquid soap to go through the hard situation of lockdowns. We also supported people with disabilities, by providing 3 wheel chairs to the vulnerable ones in Kayunga sub-county, Busaana and Kayunga town councils as well as reunion of a lady with mental illness to her family members after accessing treating in Kayunga regional referral hospital, a resident of Mansa in Kitimbwa Sub-county after being picked from Wampeewo – Gayaza Road. All their lives changed completely after accessing mobility facilities. BMCDA has been crucial for uniting people from different spheres of life without discrimination and a truck record of managing stigma against women, youth, HIV infected and affected people, key populations and ethnic minorities such as Banyala, Bakenyi, Baruuli Kuku’s in Galiraya, Busaana, Kitimbwa sub-counties of Kayunga. These were united and supported in terms of inclusion in all activities and lobbied funds for construction of mosque at Kataigwa in Galiraya sub-county.
